lesson.title: AI makes guesses
lesson.subtitle: Why a clever computer can be wrong, and how you check

video.title: AI makes guesses
video.format_note: Animated explainer, 16:9, flat Darsi colours on paper-grey backgrounds, one recurring teacher character. Narration in the lesson language; captions as separate files, never burned in.
cast: Ms Amina Bello — primary teacher, Nigeria, the student's teacher (main character)
Mr Okafor — Grade 8 science teacher, Nigeria, the student's teacher (cameo)
Narrator — the Darsi voice (warm, talking to the student)

scenes.visual: Cards: How many legs?; “Six!”; Really eight.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Yesterday a girl in my class asked a chatbot how many legs a spider has. It said six, and it sounded very sure! But a spider has eight legs. So why would a clever computer get it wrong?

scenes.visual: The title card: the course, the lesson title and subtitle, the Darsi mark.
scenes.animation: Mark pops in; the title slides up.
scenes.narration: Today: why AI makes guesses, and how you can check them.

scenes.visual: Cards joined by arrows: Millions of sentences; Words that go together; One word at a time.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: AI learns from lots and lots of examples. A chatbot has read millions of sentences. From them, it learns which words often go together. Then it guesses an answer, one word at a time.

scenes.visual: A list: Often a good guess; Sometimes wrong; Sounds sure anyway.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.on_screen_text: Sure is not the same as right
scenes.narration: A guess can be a very good guess. But sometimes it is wrong. And a chatbot doesn't feel unsure, so it sounds just as sure when it's wrong.

scenes.visual: A list: A classmate who answers fast; Usually right; Just as loud when wrong.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Think of a classmate who always answers fast. Usually they're right. But when they don't know, they answer just as fast and just as loud.

scenes.visual: The quick check: the question and its answer cards, with the speaker beside them.
scenes.animation: The speaker slides in; answer cards drop in.
scenes.narration: Quick check! A chatbot answers your question very fast, and it sounds very sure. Does that mean it's right?

scenes.visual: Cards: Fast and sure; Can still be wrong; So we check.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: No, not always. A quick, sure answer can still be a wrong guess. That's why we check.

scenes.visual: A list: Look in your school book; Ask a teacher or a grown-up; Two good sources agree.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: How do you check? Look in your school book. Ask a teacher, or a grown-up at home. And see if two good sources agree.

scenes.visual: A list: A funny poem: enjoy it; Health: check it; Safety: check it; Homework facts: check it.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Some answers matter more than others. A funny poem? Just enjoy it. But your health, your safety and your homework facts: always check.

scenes.visual: Cards: Read the answer; Right?; Wrong?; Check a book.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.on_screen_text: App lab: check the AI's answer
scenes.narration: In the app, a chatbot tells you about the river Nile. Tap each part of its answer: right, wrong, or check a book? One part sounds sure, but it's made up!

scenes.visual: The quick check: the question and its answer cards, with the speaker beside them.
scenes.animation: The speaker slides in; answer cards drop in.
scenes.narration: Your turn. A chatbot tells you a plant in the school garden is safe to eat. What do you do?

scenes.visual: The summary: It learns and guesses; Sure isn't always right; Check what matters. Takeaway: Clever, but not always right: you check.
scenes.animation: Points tick in as they are said; the takeaway slides up.
scenes.narration: Ask a grown-up first: your safety matters most. Remember: AI learns from examples and makes guesses. A sure answer can still be wrong. When it matters, check with a book or a grown-up.

scenes.visual: A list: Play with your family; Facts in a sure voice; True, false, or check?.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Try it tomorrow: play “Robot or right?” with your family. Someone reads out facts in a very sure voice, some true and some made up. Everyone else says: true, false, or let's check a book!

checkpoints.prompt: A chatbot answers fast and sounds very sure. Does that mean it's right?

options.text: No: it might still be a wrong guess

checkpoints.feedback_correct: Right! Sounding sure is not the same as being right.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite. AI guesses, and a guess can be wrong, even a fast, sure one.

checkpoints.prompt: A chatbot says a plant in the school garden is safe to eat. What do you do?

options.text: Eat it: the chatbot said so

checkpoints.feedback_correct: Yes! Your safety matters: a grown-up checks first.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite. A wrong guess about food could make you ill. Ask a grown-up first.
